Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

drcTMB 0.1.0

First release.

Models and data

  • drmTMB() fits nonlinear dose-response models with the Template Model Builder: log-logistic, logistic, Weibull (two types), log-normal, Gompertz, Michaelis-Menten, asymptotic regression, gamma, multistage, the threshold model nec, the hormesis models of Brain-Cousens and Cedergreen, the substrate inhibition model of Haldane, the exponential and power models of PROAST and BMDS, and a constant model.
  • Response distributions: gaussian, lognormal, binomial, beta-binomial, beta, poisson, negative binomial (nbinom1, nbinom2), and time-to-event data (family = "event").
  • Covariates on any parameter (fform), random effects on any parameter with the syntax of lme4 (rform), parameter links (parlink) and links of the whole curve (curvelink).
  • Correlated residuals (cor_ar1(), cor_car1(), cor_cs(), cor_exp(), cor_gaus(), cor_spher()) and variance functions (var_power(), var_exp(), var_ident()) for the gaussian and lognormal families.
  • Priors on all parameters (prior, see ?priors), with the estimates as posterior modes.
  • Starting values by linearised models or a grid search (drmTMBstart()); choice of the optimiser and a restart at the estimates (drmTMBcontrol()).
  • Data sets from the package drcData, which is not on CRAN: chickweed, daphnids, earthworms, germination, lettuce, liver.tumor, ryegrass, S.alba, selenium, TCDD and vinclozolin.

Inference

  • Wald, profile likelihood and parametric bootstrap intervals (confint(), profile(), bootstrap()); small-sample inference with t quantiles and F-based profiles for gaussian and lognormal models, as in drc.
  • Likelihood ratio, F and parametric bootstrap tests with anova().
  • Robust (sandwich) covariance, also for clustered data (vcovrobust(), argument vcov.).
  • Confidence and prediction intervals, and the parameters of the curves, with predict(); randomised quantile residuals and diagnostic plots (plot()).

Effective doses and benchmark doses

  • Effective doses of one or several curves (ed()), also with random effects, and the peak of hormesis and substrate inhibition curves (peak()).
  • Benchmark doses with the excess, additional, relative and standard deviation definitions (bmd()), conditional and marginal BMDs with random effects, and model averaging with AIC or BIC weights and bootstrap BMDLs (bmdma()).
  • Bayesian benchmark doses: the BMD parameterisation (bmdpar) with a prior on the BMD, marginal likelihoods (marglik()), Bayesian model averaging (bmdbayes()), the default priors and models of EFSA (2022) (efsapriors(), bmdefsa()), and informative PERT priors from earlier studies (fitpert()).
